title: RihalGuard Contract
description: RihalGuard v1 governance contract for enterprise AI agents. Design-time only: documents purpose, authority, risk, data handling, tool boundaries, review triggers, audit expectations, and verification checks before real integrations are added.

$schema.description: Path or URL of the JSON Schema used to validate this contract.

standard_version.description: RihalGuard standard version this contract follows.

agent_id.description: Stable lowercase identifier for the agent. Use kebab-case, for example invoice-extractor.

agent_name.description: Human-readable name shown in documentation, review notes, and demos.

version.description: Version of this specific agent or blueprint contract.

owner.description: Person or team responsible for this agent. Kept for backwards compatibility; prefer review.owner for new contracts.

last_reviewed.description: Date this contract was last reviewed. Kept for backwards compatibility; prefer review.last_reviewed for new contracts.

risk_level.description: Authority class based on the agent's worst-case technically possible action: RG-0 passive input-only, RG-1 approved lookup, RG-2 structured output or recommendation, RG-3 human-gated mutation, RG-4 limited reversible execution, RG-5 autonomous workflow.

workflow_pattern.description: Short pattern name for how the agent works, such as extract_validate_review, summarize_extract_verify, plan_review_execute, or lookup_summarize.

purpose.description: Plain-language statement of what the agent is for and who it helps.

maximum_impact.description: Worst-case action or impact the agent can cause if it fails or is misused. Classify risk by this, not by the happy path.

scope.description: Explicit authority boundary: what the agent may do and what it must never do.

allowed.description: Actions, decisions, or outputs allowed inside this agent's scope.

forbidden.description: Actions, decisions, or outputs the agent must not perform.

tool_policy.description: Tool boundary defining tools that can run, tools that need approval, and tools that are blocked.

allowed_tools.description: Tools the agent may call without extra approval when inside scope.

approval_required_tools.description: Tools that may be prepared or requested, but require human approval before execution.

blocked_tools.description: Tools or actions the agent must never execute.

fail_closed_on_unknown_tools.description: Whether runtime should block any tool not listed in this policy.

data_policy.description: Data handling rules: data classes, storage, retention, memory, isolation, and log redaction expectations.

output_policy.description: Output boundary: required format, evidence expectations, and anti-fabrication rules.

runtime_limits.description: Execution limits such as reasoning steps, timeout, cost ceiling, retries, or loop bounds.

human_review.description: Escalation and handoff policy: when human review is required and where the case should go.

audit.description: Audit expectations, including whether logs are required, append-only, and which events must be recorded.

verification.description: Checks that prove the agent's stated boundaries hold.

tests.description: Named tests, evals, or checks that should pass for this contract.

review.description: Ownership and review metadata for this contract.
